facts.raw_span: 6-month history of progressive dysarthria and dysphagia
Family history notable for a relative with memory problems after age 80
Cognitive impairment
Vertical gaze palsy
Tongue atrophy
Pyramidal signs

Almost total loss in caudate nucleus

Autoimmune encephalitis antibodies negative in serum and CSF

concepts.preferred_label: Frontotemporal dementia and parkinsonism linked to chromosome 3
support_spans: 6-month history of progressive dysarthria and dysphagia
Heterozygous pathogenic variant of TBK1 gene (p.E643del) identified by whole-exon sequencing
concepts.why: The combination of progressive dysarthria, dysphagia, cognitive impairment, vertical gaze palsy, tongue atrophy, and pyramidal signs, along with the identification of a heterozygous pathogenic variant of the TBK1 gene, supports this diagnosis.

support_spans: Severe loss of dopamine transporter binding in basal ganglia
Almost total loss in caudate nucleus
contradict_spans: Heterozygous pathogenic variant of TBK1 gene (p.E643del) identified by whole-exon sequencing
concepts.why: The presence of vertical gaze palsy and severe loss of dopamine transporter binding in the basal ganglia, particularly in the caudate nucleus, supports this diagnosis, although the genetic finding argues against it.

support_spans: 6-month history of progressive dysarthria and dysphagia
Large-amplitude, long-duration motor unit potential in frontalis, mentalis, orbicularis oculi, and genioglossus muscles
contradict_spans: Severe loss of dopamine transporter binding in basal ganglia
concepts.why: The combination of progressive dysarthria, dysphagia, tongue atrophy, and pyramidal signs, along with the electromyography findings, supports this diagnosis, although the presence of vertical gaze palsy and dopamine transporter binding loss argues against it.

rationales.F01: Progressive dysarthria and dysphagia are more typical of frontotemporal dementia and parkinsonism linked to chromosome 3 and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
rationales.F04: Vertical gaze palsy is a hallmark of progressive supranuclear palsy.
rationales.F07: Severe loss of dopamine transporter binding in basal ganglia is more typical of progressive supranuclear palsy and frontotemporal dementia and parkinsonism linked to chromosome 3.
rationales.F10: The heterozygous pathogenic variant of the TBK1 gene is a strong indicator of frontotemporal dementia and parkinsonism linked to chromosome 3.
